# Action label drift in `05-stress-ia-drift` ## 1. Drift confirmed Re-ran `crimes scan --format json` against the fixture. 13 findings; two of them are this drift, and they carry **byte-identical evidence**: | id | type | severity/conf | anchor | fix_shape | |---|---|---|---|---| | `crime_00004` | `action_label_drift` | low / 0.6 | `SeatList.tsx` | *pick one verb per action; update labels uniformly* | | `crime_00009` | `copy_ia_drift` | low / 0.6 | `SeatList.tsx` | *pick the canonical label; redirect copies to it* | Both: group `delete`, aliases `archive, delete, remove`, each in exactly 2 files. The actual source is worse than the finding summary suggests — the collision isn't only across files, it's **within** them: | File | Controls | Problem | |---|---|---| | `UserList.tsx:7-8` | `Delete user` → `/users/manage`
`Remove member` → `/users/manage` | two verbs **and** two nouns on one destination | | `TeamList.tsx:6-7` | `Archive team` → `/teams/manage`
`Delete the seat` → `/seats/manage` | a seats action rendered from the teams surface; article in the label | | `SeatList.tsx:6-7` | `Remove member` → `/seats/manage`
`Archive member` → `/seats/manage` | two verbs, one destination, one noun | Note what *didn't* fire: the `user` noun group (`user`/`member`/`seat`) is drifting just as badly, but only `member` reaches the ≥2-files bar (`user` is UserList-only, `seat` is TeamList-only), so it sits one file short of the threshold. It is real drift the scan cannot see yet. ## 2. Proposed canonical label set Don't collapse to one verb — these are three different operations, and flattening them destroys real information. Fix the *mapping*, not the vocabulary size: **Verb contract (three verbs, disjoint meanings):** - **Delete** — permanent, unrecoverable. Record is gone. - **Remove** — revokes an association. The object survives elsewhere. - **Archive** — reversible. Hidden from default views, restorable. **Noun contract:** singular, no article, matches the destination's own vocabulary (`/users/*` → user, `/teams/*` → team, `/seats/*` → member). **Resulting labels — one control per surface:** | Surface | Canonical label | href | |---|---|---| | Users | `Delete user` | `/users/manage` | | Teams | `Archive team` | `/teams/manage` | | Seats | `Remove member` | `/seats/manage` | Verified: this clears both findings (13 → 11) and doesn't push the `user` noun group over its threshold. ## 3. Refactor first: `UserList.tsx` Not because it's the anchor (SeatList is, purely by lexical sort), but because it's the only file where the right label is unambiguous without a product decision. `Delete user` on `/users/manage` is clearly a hard delete; `Remove member` on the same href is a stray duplicate you can drop on sight. No one needs to be consulted. The other two require a decision you can't make from the code: - `SeatList` — is `Archive member` a reversible state or just a softer word for `Remove`? If the two controls do the same thing, one is dead; if not, both need distinct destinations, because they currently share `/seats/manage`. - `TeamList` — `Delete the seat` belongs on the seats surface. Moving it is an IA change, not a copy change, and it interacts with `concept_alias_drift` (`crime_00002`) on the tenant group. Order: **UserList** (mechanical) → **SeatList** (one product question) → **TeamList** (IA move). Ship all three in one commit. The anchor is `allFiles[0]` after a lexical sort (`action-label-drift.ts:126-127`), so if you land SeatList alone the anchor slides to TeamList, the fingerprint changes from `action_label_drift::src/components/SeatList.tsx::` to `…TeamList.tsx::`, and your baseline reports one resolved finding plus one *new* one. ## 4. Change → finding mapping Every change above satisfies **both** findings simultaneously, because on this fixture they are the same finding twice: | Change | `action_label_drift` | `copy_ia_drift` | |---|---|---| | Drop `Remove member` from `UserList` | ✅ `remove` falls to 1 file | ✅ same | | Collapse `SeatList` to `Remove member` | ✅ `archive` falls to 1 file | ✅ same | | Move `Delete the seat` off `TeamList` | ✅ `delete` falls to 1 file | ✅ same | ## 5. How the two detectors differ — and why they don't, here They share one implementation. `copy-ia-drift.ts:30-37` calls `analyse(...)` from `action-label-drift.ts:71` with the same `ACTION_GROUPS` and one extra option, `restrictToJsxLabel: true`. That flag does two things (`action-label-drift.ts:91`, `:99`): 1. Keeps only labels whose `kind` starts with `jsx_` — drops `document_title`, `metadata_title`, `use_title`. 2. Skips the `navEntries` loop entirely — nav labels and nav attributes don't contribute. So `action_label_drift` reads the whole IA label+nav surface; `copy_ia_drift` reads pure JSX UI copy. Everything else — the ≥3-aliases-each-in-≥2-files gate (`:122-124`), severity (`:128`), confidence 0.6, the anchor rule — is identical. **On this fixture the broader surface contributes nothing.** All six delete-group hits come from `NavItem label="…"` props in the three components, which are `jsx_label` signals — the intersection of both input sets. `src/nav.ts` and the route files contain no delete-group token, so `action_label_drift`'s extra reach adds zero hits. Same group, same aliases, same files, same anchor, same severity. The only observable difference in the JSON is `fix_shape` and `detector_id`. That's the fixture doing its job: it proves the two detectors stay in sync. It does not exercise the case that distinguishes them — a `delete`-group verb sitting in `nav.ts` or in a non-JSX string prop would fire `action_label_drift` alone. Worth adding if this fixture is meant to discriminate rather than just co-fire. ## 6. Caveat on treating the finding as your success signal I tested each single-file deletion independently. **All three clear both findings.** Deleting only `Delete the seat` from `TeamList` silences the scan while `UserList` still ships `Delete user` and `Remove member` on the same href — the most blatant drift in the repo, now invisible. The gate is ≥3 aliases each in ≥2 files; removing any one alias's second file drops you to 2 and the finding vanishes. A naive collapse-everything-to-`Remove` also passes, and leaves `SeatList` with two identical `Remove member` controls. Green scan ≠ fixed. Write the verb contract from §2 into a copy guide (`AGENTS.md` would also address `crime_00001`, which flags that this repo ships no agent-readable instructions at all — an agent editing these files today has nothing telling it which verb to pick).
